t: A much smaller defending force of foreigners and citizens held about 20 km of walls against a much larger Ottoman army and its cannon, and no relief from Western Europe arrived in time.
The sack was severe. Thousands were killed and, by one count, around 30,000 people were enslaved; Mehmed ordered the looting stopped and issued a proclamation to those who had hidden or fled.
Many modern historians treat the fall as the end of the medieval period, and the capture of the last Roman capital as the end of the Roman Empire.
dyk: On 22 April Mehmed had ships hauled on greased logs across the hill at Galata into the Golden Horn, bypassing the chain across its mouth that the defenders had counted on to keep Ottoman ships out.
ev: Mehmed II builds the fortress of Rumeli Hisari on the Bosphorus, and Constantine XI declares church union valid on 12 December
Giovanni Giustiniani arrives in January with about 700 men and is given command of the land walls
The Ottoman army encamps outside the city on 2 April and the siege begins on 6 April
Mehmed has his ships dragged into the Golden Horn on 22 April, and the fire-ship attack of 28 April fails
Ottoman mining from mid-May is met by counter-mines, and Constantine refuses Mehmed's offer of terms on 21 May
Shortly after midnight on 29 May the final assault begins, Giustiniani is wounded and the walls are overwhelmed
Looting and enslavement follow for part of three days, after which Mehmed halts them and has Hagia Sophia made a mosque
Mystras in the Morea, held by Constantine's brothers, falls to the Ottomans

f.date: Siege of 53 days from 6 April to 29 May 1453; the city was taken on 29 May
f.place: Constantinople, now Istanbul, on the Bosphorus; the fighting centred on the Theodosian land walls, especially the Mesoteichion and the Blachernae district, and on the Golden Horn
f.sides: The Byzantine Empire under Emperor Constantine XI Palaiologos, with Genoese, Venetian and other foreign help: about 7,000 men, 2,000 of them foreigners by one count, and under 8,000 by Sphrantzes' census. The Ottoman Empire under Sultan Mehmed II: some 50,000 to 80,000 men by recent studies, against 160,000 to 300,000 in Western witnesses.
f.outcome: The Ottomans took the city after a final assault on 29 May. It was looted for part of three days, many of its people were killed or enslaved, and Mehmed made it his capital. Constantine XI's fate is unknown.
